# docling.rs

**docling.rs** converts documents — PDF, Office, HTML, scans, audio — into Markdown, docling JSON and the other shapes an LLM or a RAG pipeline can read. It is a Rust port of IBM's [docling](https://github.com/docling-project/docling): the same output, byte-for-byte, from one static binary. No Python, no PyTorch. Pulling text out of a PDF is easy. Keeping its *structure* — headings in order, tables as tables, scanned pages read — takes layout analysis, table recognition and OCR. docling has the models for that, and a Python stack to match. docling.rs runs the same models from a single binary: PDF 4.3× faster than Python docling at under half the RAM, Office and HTML 20–60× faster, and tables that survive — cell recall 0.94 where MarkItDown gets 0.31 ([numbers](#conformance-with-microsoft-markitdown), [method](./docs/PDF_CONFORMANCE.md#performance--review--profiling-notes)). **Coming from [MarkItDown](https://github.com/microsoft/markitdown)?** `pip install docling-rs`, swap one import — `from docling_rs.markitdown import MarkItDown` — and keep its API, every format it converts included, with real layout analysis, tables and OCR behind it: [guide](./docs/MARKITDOWN.md), [measured side by side](#conformance-with-microsoft-markitdown). **Coming from [Marker](https://github.com/datalab-to/marker)?** `pip install docling-rs`, swap the imports — `from docling_rs.marker.converters.pdf import PdfConverter` — and keep its API: `create_model_dict`, `text_from_rendered`, the JSON block tree, chunks, `marker_single`'s CLI and output layout, with docling's layout analysis, TableFormer and OCR behind it and no PyTorch or inference server: [guide](./docs/MARKER.md), [measured side by side](#conformance-with-marker). **Coming from [MinerU](https://github.com/opendatalab/MinerU)?** `pip install docling-rs`, swap the imports — `from docling_rs.mineru.parser import parse` — and keep MinerU 4's SDK: `ParseResult`, `markdown()`, the Middle JSON, Content Lists and Structured Content, `save()`'s layout and `mineru-kit parse`, with docling's layout analysis, TableFormer and OCR behind it and no DocVortex or llama.cpp: [guide](./docs/MINERU.md), [measured side by side](#conformance-with-mineru). ## Install ```bash # CLI + models (Linux x64/arm64/s390x + macOS arm64 prebuilt; builds from source elsewhere) curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/docling-project/docling.rs/master/scripts/install/install.sh | bash docling-rs example.pdf # Markdown on stdout # or from crates.io; --cli puts the models where the installed binary looks cargo install docling-cli curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/docling-project/docling.rs/master/scripts/install/download_dependencies.sh | sh -s -- --cli pip install docling-rs # Python — drop-in for docling's, MarkItDown's, Marker's and MinerU's APIs npm install docling.rs # Node.js / Bun cargo add docling # Rust library # containers, models baked in (-cuda variants for NVIDIA) docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/data" ghcr.io/docling-project/docling-rs paper.pdf docker run -p 127.0.0.1:5001:5001 ghcr.io/docling-project/docling-rs-serve ``` Office, HTML, Markdown and e-mail need no models. PDF, images and audio need the ONNX models (layout, OCR, TableFormer, Whisper; under 1 GB): `install.sh`, `--cli` and the containers bring them along; with `pip`, run `python -c "import docling_rs; docling_rs.download_models()"` once; with `npm` or a checkout, run `download_dependencies.sh` where you convert ([details](#getting-the-ml-models)). Windows: [`docs/WINDOWS.md`](./docs/WINDOWS.md). **▶ [Try it in your browser](https://docling-project.github.io/docling.rs/)** first — the converter as wasm, OCR included; nothing leaves your device. ## Use ```bash docling-rs report.pdf > report.md # Markdown (streamed page by page) docling-rs report.pdf --to json # docling JSON; also html, text, latex, dclx, chunks, images docling-rs --input ./docs --output ./out # a directory tree; --jobs N in parallel docling-rs https://example.com/paper.pdf # URLs, data: URIs and stdin (`-`) too docling-rs https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ID # a YouTube video: title, description, caption transcript (--to vtt keeps the timing) docling-rs --help # every flag: OCR, page ranges, images, enrichment, redaction … ``` ```python from docling_rs import DocumentConverter # was: from docling.document_converter import … doc = DocumentConverter().convert("report.pdf").document print(doc.export_to_markdown()) ``` ```js import { convertFileAsync } from 'docling.rs' const { content } = await convertFileAsync('report.pdf', { to: 'markdown' }) ``` ```rust use docling::{DocumentConverter, SourceDocument}; let result = DocumentConverter::new().convert(SourceDocument::from_file("report.pdf")?)?; println!("{}", result.document.export_to_markdown()); ``` ```bash curl -F file=@report.pdf 'localhost:5001/v1/convert?to=md' # the server; OpenAPI at /openapi.yaml ``` Same options, same outputs on every surface — every option in [`docs/OPTIONS.md`](./docs/OPTIONS.md). ## Highlights - **From Python docling:** `from docling_rs import DocumentConverter`; `result.document` is a genuine `DoclingDocument` ([migration notes](./crates/docling-py/README.md#migrating-from-python-docling)). - **Every docling format, and a few it lacks** — the table under [Status](#status), each validated against live docling ([Conformance](#conformance-with-python-docling)). - **Every output docling has:** Markdown (docling's, or a stricter dialect), docling JSON, HTML, plain text, DocLang, LaTeX, Pandoc AST (→ DOCX, EPUB, Typst… through pandoc), WebVTT subtitles, RAG chunks and page images ([output formats](./crates/docling/README.md#output-formats)). - **From any language:** Rust, Python, Node.js / Bun, the browser (wasm, fully client-side), C, C++, C#, Go, Java and Swift through one C header, any HTTP client, the shell ([Integration](#integration--using-doclingrs-from-your-language)). - **A drop-in server for docling-serve:** Open WebUI uses it as its Docling content-extraction engine — point *Docling Server URL* at `http://:5001` — and n8n, Dify and LangChain clients work unchanged ([`docling-rs serve`](#http-conversion-api--docling-rs-serve), [Open WebUI setup](./crates/docling-serve/README.md#open-webui)). - **AI agents (MCP):** `docling-rs mcp` gives Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor or VS Code MarkItDown's `convert_to_markdown` tool, plus `convert` for JSON, chunks and the rest — `uvx docling-rs-mcp`, or `claude mcp add docling -- docling-rs mcp` ([MCP server](#mcp-server--docling-rs-mcp)). - **LangChain:** `pip install "docling-rs[langchain]"` — langchain-docling's `DoclingLoader` on the Rust engine, one import to swap ([details](./crates/docling-py/README.md#langchain)). - **AutoGen:** `pip install "docling-rs[autogen]"` — `DoclingIndexer` fills any AutoGen memory with chunks that carry their pages, `DoclingConvertTool` lets an agent read documents ([details](./crates/docling-py/README.md#autogen)). - **Your own formats:** register a backend for a format docling.rs does not read — or to read one of its formats your way — from Rust, Python (`@docling_rs.register_backend(extensions=["rtf2"])`, and MarkItDown's `register_converter` and plugins) or Node.js, ahead of the built-in formats ([pluggable backends](./crates/docling/README.md#pluggable-backends)). - **RAG:** `docling-rag` — chunk, embed and search with a REST API and a web UI ([RAG subsystem](#rag-subsystem)). - **Runs where you are:** Linux x64 / arm64 / s390x, macOS (Apple Silicon) and Windows prebuilt (CLI, wheels, npm), Intel macs from source, containers for amd64 and arm64; NVIDIA CUDA and TensorRT, DirectML, CoreML and WebGPU in the browser as opt-in accelerators ([GPU](./docs/MODELS.md#gpu-execution-providers-optional-off-by-default), [IBM Z](./docs/IBMZ.md)). Developed with **Claude Code** and _[TENET](https://github.com/artiz/tenet/tree/master)_ (minimalistic AI-driven development framework). ## Status Every format in docling's pipeline converts — plus a few docling lacks. A file with no or an unknown extension, stdin, an upload or a `data:` URL is typed by its content (`InputFormat::detect`, `docling_rs.detect_format`, `detectFormat`: the packages, the OLE files, PDF, images, audio and video, iWork, XML, JSON, notebooks, messages, …), and a file that fails under its extension is checked by content and converted as what it really is, with a warning. | Category | Formats | |---|---| | Text & markup | Markdown, AsciiDoc, HTML, MHTML, LaTeX (multi-file arXiv projects, math, tables); plain text and source code (`.py`, `.yaml`, `.log`, … — any text file, as a code block or paragraphs), generic JSON / JSON Lines and XML (kept as code blocks); RSS / Atom / RDF feeds (`.rss`, `.atom`, `.rdf` or a bare `.xml`: the feed's title, each item's heading, date and body); Jupyter notebooks (`.ipynb`: markdown cells, code cells in the kernel's language, outputs on request) | | Word processing | DOCX, Word 97–2004 `.doc` (and Word 6/95, 1.x/2.0), ODT, OpenOffice / StarWriter, AbiWord, WordPerfect, MS Works, EPUB, RTF | | Presentations | PPTX, PowerPoint 97–2003, ODP, OpenOffice / StarImpress | | Spreadsheets | XLSX, XLSB, Excel 97–2004, ODS, CSV / TSV, dBase, DIF, SYLK, Lotus 1-2-3, Quattro Pro, MS Works | | Diagrams · Apple iWork | Visio, SVG · Pages, Numbers, Keynote | | PDF & images | PDF (layout, TableFormer, OCR), PNG, JPEG, TIFF, BMP, WebP, GIF, HEIC (opt-in), METS/GBS scans, DjVu | | XML · docling native | JATS, USPTO, XBRL, DocLang · docling JSON, DocTags, DCLX | | Email · subtitles · mainframe | `.eml`, Outlook `.msg` · WebVTT · EBCDIC records through a COBOL copybook | | Audio · video | WAV, MP3, M4A, AAC, OGG, FLAC; MP4, AVI, MOV, MKV, WebM, MPEG — local Whisper or Parakeet, plus scene frames from video; a YouTube watch URL — the video's title, description and caption transcript as timed items (`--asr-lang` picks the language) | Every extension, with what each backend does: [`docs/MIGRATION.md`](./docs/MIGRATION.md#every-extension-by-category).
Installing ffmpeg (optional — only for video frame sampling) Any ffmpeg ≥ 4.x on `PATH` works; docling.rs shells out to the binary and parses its output, so no dev headers/libraries are needed. - **Debian/Ubuntu**: `sudo apt-get install ffmpeg` - **Fedora**: `sudo dnf install ffmpeg-free` (or `ffmpeg` from RPM Fusion) - **Alpine**: `apk add ffmpeg` - **macOS**: `brew install ffmpeg` - **Windows**: `winget install ffmpeg` (or `choco install ffmpeg`, or `scoop install ffmpeg`). Installing from a downloaded zip ([gyan.dev](https://www.gyan.dev/ffmpeg/builds/) / [BtbN](https://github.com/BtbN/FFmpeg-Builds/releases)) also works — either add the extracted `bin\` folder to `PATH`, or skip `PATH` entirely and point `DOCLING_FFMPEG` at the exe: `set DOCLING_FFMPEG=C:\tools\ffmpeg\bin\ffmpeg.exe` Check with `ffmpeg -version`. `DOCLING_FFMPEG` overrides the binary used on any OS; the docling-rs-serve Docker image ships ffmpeg preinstalled. A trimmed, decode-only build (`--disable-everything --enable-…`) works too (#853); docling.rs needs only: the `file` protocol; the demuxers of your containers (`mov` for mp4/mov/m4v, `matroska` for mkv/webm, `avi`, `mpeg`); the video decoders of your tracks (`h264`, `hevc`, `vp8`, `vp9`, `av1`, `mpeg4`, `mpeg2video`, …) with their parsers; the filters `select`, `metadata`, `fps`, `scale`, `showinfo`; the encoders `png` and `wrapped_avframe`; the muxers `image2` and `null`. No audio component is used — the transcript is decoded in Rust — and the scene scan maps the video stream alone. Missing a component, ffmpeg fails the scene scan (`Encoder not found`, `Invalid argument`) and the video converts as transcript only; `DOCLING_RS_DEBUG=1` shows the message.
## Conformance with Microsoft MarkItDown [MarkItDown](https://github.com/microsoft/markitdown) converts the same kinds of documents to Markdown for LLMs. Measured side by side — MarkItDown 0.1.8 (`markitdown[all]`) and docling.rs 2.33.0 (release build), 4 vCPU, no GPU — on this repository's test corpus and on MarkItDown's own OCR test set ([`scripts/conformance/markitdown_compare.py`](./scripts/conformance/markitdown_compare.py)): | Corpus (files) | MarkItDown, warm | docling.rs, warm | Cold CLI call, MarkItDown / docling.rs | Word F1 | Table-cell recall | Heading recall | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | DOCX (38) | 4.22 s | **0.44 s** | 1102 / **14** ms | 0.93 / **1.00** | 0.81 / **1.00** | 0.78 / **1.00** | | PPTX (8) | 0.30 s | **0.02 s** | 974 / **6** ms | 0.81 / **0.97** | 0.62 / **1.00** | 0.86 / **1.00** | | XLSX (14) | 0.87 s | **0.15 s** | 849 / **7** ms | 0.60 / **0.95** | 0.78 / **0.98** | — ¹ | | HTML (32) | 0.34 s | **0.05 s** | 900 / **6** ms | 0.98 / **1.00** | 0.89 / **1.00** | 0.96 / **1.00** | | CSV (9) | 0.04 s | **0.01 s** | 900 / **4** ms | 1.00 / 1.00 | 0.78 / **1.00** | — | | EPUB (1) | 0.06 s | **0.01 s** | 897 / **10** ms | 0.99 / **1.00** | — | 1.00 / 1.00 | | PDF (18), full layout + tables + OCR | **7.6 s** | 38.4 s | 984 / **830** ms | 0.63 / **0.997** | 0.31 / **0.94** | 0.00 / **0.91** | | PDF (18), text layer only (`--text-layer-only`) | 7.6 s | **0.5 s** | — | 0.63 / **0.97** | 0.31 / 0.00 | 0.00 / 0.00 | Accuracy is scored against Python docling's groundtruth, which favours docling.rs by construction; the timings do not depend on it. Text drawn into images (MarkItDown's own OCR test set) reads at 1.00 with docling.rs' local OCR, against 0.00–0.33 for MarkItDown without an LLM. Method, caveats and the full OCR comparison: [`docs/MARKITDOWN.md`](./docs/MARKITDOWN.md#how-the-comparison-is-scored). ## Conformance with Marker [Marker](https://github.com/datalab-to/marker) (datalab's `marker-pdf`) converts PDFs and, through a PDF render, Office files to Markdown for LLMs with a layout model and OCR. Measured side by side — Marker 2.0.0 (`marker-pdf[full]`, its CPU default `fast` mode, llama.cpp for its OCR) and docling.rs 2.46.2 (release build), 4 vCPU, no GPU — on this repository's test corpus ([`scripts/conformance/marker_compare.py`](./scripts/conformance/marker_compare.py)): | Corpus (files) | Marker, warm | docling.rs, warm | Cold CLI call, Marker / docling.rs | Peak RSS, Marker (client + servers) / docling.rs | Word F1 | Table-cell recall | Heading recall | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | PDF (18), full layout + tables + OCR | 1312 s | **41 s** | 22.0 s / **1.0 s** | 10.5 GB / **3.1 GB** | 0.93 / **0.997** | 0.41 / **0.94** | 0.66 / **0.91** | | PDF (18), text layer only (`--text-layer-only`) | 1312 s | **0.44 s** | — | — / 79 MB | 0.93 / **0.97** | 0.41 / 0.00 | 0.66 / 0.00 | | DOCX (38) | 654 s (1 failed) | **0.56 s** | 23.4 s / **15 ms** | 8.6 GB / **41 MB** | 0.89 / **1.00** | 0.57 / **1.00** | 0.73 / **1.00** | | PPTX (8) | 3.4 s (3 failed) | **0.02 s** | 21.8 s / **9 ms** | 2.6 GB / **20 MB** | 0.49 / **0.97** | 0.41 / **1.00** | 0.43 / **1.00** | | XLSX (14) | 164 s (2 failed) | **0.24 s** | 22.8 s / **10 ms** | 12.9 GB / **53 MB** | 0.64 / **0.95** | 0.57 / **0.98** | — ¹ | | HTML (32) | 1514 s | **0.06 s** | 29 min ² / **8 ms** | 8.8 GB / **21 MB** | 0.94 / **1.00** | 0.50 / **1.00** | 0.84 / **1.00** | | EPUB (1) | 10.5 s | **0.02 s** | 60.7 s / **13 ms** | 6.8 GB / **19 MB** | 0.98 / **1.00** | — | 1.00 / 1.00 | A failed file scores 0. ¹ Only one XLSX groundtruth carries a heading. ² The median HTML file needs OCR in Marker: a cold call starts its llama.cpp server and loads the 1.2 GB OCR model first. Accuracy is scored against Python docling's groundtruth, which favours docling.rs by construction; the timings and memory do not depend on it. Marker reads Office files, HTML and EPUB by rendering them to PDF and running its vision models on the render; on CPU every page its text check flags goes through a 1.2 GB vision-language OCR model in a llama.cpp server that `pip install marker-pdf` does not bring (without it 4 PDFs, 9 DOCX, 10 HTML and the EPUB fail outright). Peak RSS counts Marker's client and its inference servers. Marker's `balanced` mode (its published benchmarks) needs a GPU. Method, caveats and the API map: [`docs/MARKER.md`](./docs/MARKER.md#how-the-comparison-is-scored). ## Conformance with MinerU [MinerU](https://github.com/opendatalab/MinerU) (OpenDataLab) converts PDFs, images and Office files to Markdown and JSON for LLMs in four tiers — `flash` (text layer, no models), `basic` (ONNX layout / table / OCR models), `standard` and `advanced` (a vision-language model through llama.cpp). Measured side by side — MinerU 4.0.12 and docling.rs 2.46.2 (release build), 4 vCPU, no GPU — on this repository's test corpus ([`scripts/conformance/mineru_compare.py`](./scripts/conformance/mineru_compare.py)): | Corpus (files) | MinerU `flash`, warm | MinerU `basic`, warm | docling.rs, warm | Cold CLI call, MinerU `flash` / `basic` / docling.rs | Peak RSS, MinerU `flash` / `basic` / docling.rs | Word F1 (`flash` / `basic` / docling.rs) | Table-cell recall | Heading recall | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | PDF (18), full layout + tables + OCR | 22.3 s | 123 s (+ 67 s model load) | **44.0 s** | 3.6 s / 6.5 s / **1.2 s** | 1.4 GB / 4.6 GB / 3.1 GB | 0.87 / 0.74 / **0.997** | 0.28 / 0.44 / **0.94** | 0.57 / 0.58 / **0.91** | | PDF (18), text layer only (`--text-layer-only`) | 22.3 s | — | **0.69 s** | — / — / — | — / — / 80 MB | 0.87 / — / **0.97** | 0.28 / — / 0.00 | 0.57 / — / 0.00 | | DOCX (38) | 6.36 s | flash only | **0.59 s** | 2355 ms / — / **15 ms** | 179 MB / — / **41 MB** | 0.97 / — / **1.00** | 0.82 / — / **1.00** | 0.96 / — / **1.00** | | PPTX (8) | 0.21 s (1 failed) | flash only | **0.05 s** | 2199 ms / — / **9 ms** | 122 MB / — / **20 MB** | 0.79 / — / **0.97** | 0.91 / — / **1.00** | 1.00 / — / 1.00 | | XLSX (14) | 0.68 s | flash only | **0.19 s** | 978 ms / — / **14 ms** | 140 MB / — / **55 MB** | 0.83 / — / **0.95** | 0.77 / — / **0.98** | — ¹ | | HTML (32) | 0.89 s | flash only | **0.10 s** | 2015 ms / — / **10 ms** | 157 MB / — / **21 MB** | 0.94 / — / **1.00** | 0.81 / — / **1.00** | 0.96 / — / **1.00** | | EPUB (1) | 0.09 s | flash only | **0.02 s** | 1909 ms / — / **16 ms** | 99 MB / — / **19 MB** | 1.00 / 1.00 | — | 1.00 / 1.00 | A failed file scores 0. ¹ Only one XLSX groundtruth carries a heading. Accuracy is scored against Python docling's groundtruth, which favours docling.rs by construction; the timings and memory do not depend on it. MinerU parses Office files, HTML and EPUB at `flash` only; `basic` is its model tier on CPU; its `standard` tier (a 1.2 B vision-language model through llama.cpp) took 138 s for one page on this CPU and is not in the table. Method, caveats and the API map: [`docs/MINERU.md`](./docs/MINERU.md#how-the-comparison-is-scored). ## Conformance with Python docling Every declarative format is compared against the live library — Markdown byte for byte, JSON structurally (every key and value but `origin`/`version` and re-encoded image bytes). Latest sweep, docling **2.129.0** (`scripts/conformance/full_conformance.py`; ✅ all = every file matches): | Format | Files | Markdown | JSON | Format | Files | Markdown | JSON | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | DOCX | 38 | ✅ all | ✅ all | iWork Pages | 1 | ✅ all | ✅ all | | HTML | 32 | ✅ all | 31 | iWork Keynote | 5 | ✅ all | ✅ all | | PPTX | 8 | ✅ all | ✅ all | EBCDIC | 3 | ✅ all | ✅ all | | XLSX | 14 | 13 ² | 13 ² | JATS | 7 | ✅ all | ✅ all | | ODF | 7 | ✅ all | ✅ all | DocLang | 15 | ✅ all | ✅ all | | CSV | 9 | ✅ all | 6 | AsciiDoc | 5 | ✅ all | ✅ all | | Markdown | 11 | ✅ all | 6 | USPTO | 9 | ✅ all | ✅ all | | DeepSeek-OCR Markdown | 3 | ✅ all | n/a | EPUB | 1 | ✅ all | ✅ all | | WebVTT | 4 | ✅ all | ✅ all | LaTeX | 8 | ✅ all | 7 ¹ | | Email (`.eml`) | 2 | ✅ all | ✅ all | | | | | ¹ `1706.03762`: one `tabular`'s cells carry consistent `row_span`/`col_span` where upstream writes the span into the offsets only; PDF figures carry no image payload (upstream renders them with pypdfium2). ² `xlsx_02_sample_sales_data`: 20 date cells print by docling PR #4628's number-format rules (#634), which the released docling does not apply yet. The residuals, with the exact files: [`docs/MIGRATION.md`](./docs/MIGRATION.md). The PDF/image pipeline is pinned by a deterministic snapshot baseline and scored against docling's groundtruth in [`docs/PDF_CONFORMANCE.md`](./docs/PDF_CONFORMANCE.md). ## Performance One fixture per format through published Python docling and the Rust release binary (`scripts/test/performance.sh`); docling ÷ docling.rs, so bigger means Rust wins by more. | File | Size | Peak-memory ratio | CPU ratio | Warm-conversion speedup | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | `picture_classification.pdf` (PDF) | 208 KB | **6.5× less** | 0.8× | 10.6× | | `docx_rich_tables_01.docx` (DOCX) | 3.1 MB | **39× less** | 1.2× | 19× | | `wiki_duck.html` (HTML) | 240 KB | **57× less** | 1.3× | 47× | | `elife-56337.nxml` (JATS XML) | 180 KB | **59× less** | 1.2× | 10× | | `xlsx_04_inflated.xlsx` (XLSX) | 168 KB | **51× less** | 0.9× | 18× | | `powerpoint_with_image.pptx` (PPTX) | 80 KB | **55× less** | 1.2× | 3.1× | | `wiki.md` (Markdown) | 8 KB | **57× less** | 1.2× | 1.2× | | `csv-comma.csv` (CSV) | 4 KB | **64× less** | 1.2× | 0.6× † | † A 4 KB CSV converts in microseconds, so Rust's own process startup dominates its number; end to end it is 870× faster. Declarative formats hold a few MB against docling's ~750 MB (it imports torch even for them) and finish 300–870× sooner end to end; the PDF peaks at 0.37 GB against 2.4 GB and converts 28.5× faster end to end. Where the time goes, and what was measured not to help: [`docs/PDF_CONFORMANCE.md`](./docs/PDF_CONFORMANCE.md#where-the-time-goes). ## Integration — using docling.rs from your language One engine, several front doors, the same options and outputs everywhere. | You write… | Use | Install | |---|---|---| | Rust | the [`docling`](./crates/docling/README.md) crate | `cargo add docling` | | a shell / CI job | the [`docling-rs` CLI](./crates/docling-cli/README.md), batch mode included | release binaries · `cargo install docling-cli` · `ghcr.io/docling-project/docling-rs` | | anything that speaks HTTP | [`docling-serve`](./crates/docling-serve/README.md), OpenAPI 3.1 | `ghcr.io/docling-project/docling-rs-serve` · `cargo install docling-serve` | | Node.js / Bun / Electron | [`docling.rs`](./crates/docling-node/README.md), an N-API addon | `npm i docling.rs` (`docling.rs-cuda`) | | Python | [`docling-rs`](./crates/docling-py/README.md): docling's, MarkItDown's, Marker's and MinerU's APIs | `pip install docling-rs` (`docling-rs-cuda`) | | LangChain / LlamaIndex | [`DoclingLoader`](./crates/docling-py/README.md#langchain) (langchain-docling's API) · [`DoclingReader`](./crates/docling-py/README.md#llamaindex) (llama-index-readers-docling's API) | `pip install langchain-docling-rs` · `pip install llama-index-readers-docling-rs` | | the browser / Tauri / a PWA | [`docling.rs-wasm`](./crates/docling-wasm/README.md), fully client-side | `npm i docling.rs-wasm` | | C, C++, C#, Go, Java, Swift, Zig | [`docling-ffi`](./crates/docling-ffi/README.md): one `docling.h` | release archives `docling-ffi--` | **Rust** when you're already in Cargo; the **CLI** for scripts and batch jobs; **serve** when several services share one warm pipeline; **Node / Python** in-process; **wasm** when the document must not leave the user's machine; **FFI** for anything that can call C. ## Rust API ```rust use docling::{DocumentConverter, SourceDocument}; let converter = DocumentConverter::new(); let result = converter.convert(SourceDocument::from_file("input.md")?)?; println!("{}", result.document.export_to_markdown()); // Markdown println!("{}", result.document.export_to_json()); // docling DoclingDocument JSON ``` Every conversion knob is one serializable struct, `docling::ConvertOptions`, filled the same way by every surface ([`docs/OPTIONS.md`](./docs/OPTIONS.md)). The [library guide](./crates/docling/README.md) covers the output formats, error handling, chunking, image extraction, streaming, OCR, the PDF switches, the remote VLM pipeline and registering your own backends (#680). ## HTTP conversion API — `docling-rs serve` [`docling-serve`](./crates/docling-serve/README.md) exposes the converter over HTTP with one warm PDF/image pipeline shared across requests (repeat PDFs skip the model load), streamed Markdown, batches, ZIP inputs, async jobs, an interactive test form at `GET /` and an OpenAPI 3.1 description at `GET /openapi.yaml`. It also serves Python docling-serve's routes, so Open WebUI, n8n, Dify and LangChain clients work unchanged. ```bash docker run -p 127.0.0.1:5001:5001 ghcr.io/docling-project/docling-rs-serve curl -F file=@paper.pdf localhost:5001/v1/convert # Markdown curl -F file=@report.docx 'localhost:5001/v1/convert?to=json' # docling JSON curl -F file=@a.pdf -F file=@b.docx localhost:5001/v1/convert # a batch ``` Request options, server flags, async jobs, the docling-serve routes and the Open WebUI setup: [`crates/docling-serve/README.md`](./crates/docling-serve/README.md); containers and sizing: [`docs/DEPLOYMENT.md`](./docs/DEPLOYMENT.md). ## MCP server — `docling-rs mcp` `docling-rs mcp` is a [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) server in the default `docling-rs` binary and image. Agents get MarkItDown's `convert_to_markdown(uri)` tool — same name and contract, so a `markitdown-mcp` setup switches by changing the command — plus `convert(uri, to, options)` and `list_input_formats()`. ```json { "mcpServers": { "docling": { "command": "docling-rs", "args": ["mcp", "--root", "/Users/me/Documents"] } } } ``` ```bash claude mcp add docling -- docling-rs mcp --root ~/Documents # Claude Code uvx docling-rs-mcp --root ~/Documents # the same server from PyPI ``` Local reads stay under `--root`; URLs need `--allow-url-fetch`. Listed in the [official MCP registry](https://registry.modelcontextprotocol.io/v0/servers?search=io.github.docling-project/docling-rs) and on [Smithery](https://smithery.ai/servers/artem-kustikov/docling-rs). The PyPI launcher, Docker, Streamable HTTP (`--http`), the security model and memory behaviour: [`crates/docling-cli/README.md`](./crates/docling-cli/README.md#mcp-server--docling-rs-mcp). ## RAG subsystem [`crates/docling-rag`](./crates/docling-rag/README.md) turns documents into chunks, embeds them (Ollama, Gemini or a local ONNX model), stores them (SQLite + sqlite-vec or PostgreSQL + pgvector) and searches them — hybrid, multi-query and HyDE retrieval, an evaluation harness, a REST API and a built-in search UI. ## In the browser — `docling-wasm` The declarative converters and the PDF text layer compile to WebAssembly: `npm i docling.rs-wasm`, then `convert(bytes, filename, to)` runs **fully client-side** — no server, a ~3.4 MB gzipped module, optional in-browser OCR. Details and the demo page: [`crates/docling-wasm`](./crates/docling-wasm/README.md). ## Node.js, Python and C - **Node.js / Bun** — [`docling.rs`](./crates/docling-node/README.md) on npm, a prebuilt N-API addon: sync and async conversion, streaming, chunking, ZIP batches, a warm `Pipeline`. - **Python** — [`docling-rs`](./crates/docling-py/README.md) on PyPI (`docling-rs-cuda` for NVIDIA): docling's `DocumentConverter` with a genuine docling-core `DoclingDocument`, MarkItDown's API, and the LangChain and AutoGen integrations. - **C ABI** — [`docling-ffi`](./crates/docling-ffi/README.md): one library and one `docling.h` for C, C++, C#/.NET, Go, Java, Swift and Zig, prebuilt in every published release. ## Deploy in a container | Image | What it is | |---|---| | [`ghcr.io/docling-project/docling-rs-serve`](https://github.com/docling-project/docling.rs/pkgs/container/docling-rs-serve) | the HTTP API, models baked in (`linux/amd64`, `linux/arm64`) | | [`ghcr.io/docling-project/docling-rs`](https://github.com/docling-project/docling.rs/pkgs/container/docling-rs) | the CLI, entrypoint `docling-rs`, working directory `/data` | | `…-serve-cuda` · `…-rs-cuda` | the same on CUDA 13 + cuDNN 9 (`linux/amd64`) | Compose files (standalone, Caddy TLS, CUDA), environment variables, sizing and observability: [`docs/DEPLOYMENT.md`](./docs/DEPLOYMENT.md). ## Getting the ML models The PDF/image pipeline needs ONNX models — RT-DETR layout, PP-OCR, and TableFormer — and audio needs Whisper. `download_dependencies.sh` fetches them from this repository's [releases](https://github.com/docling-project/docling.rs/releases) into `./.models`, where every surface looks (`--cli`: beside a cargo-installed binary instead): ```bash scripts/install/download_dependencies.sh # from a checkout curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/docling-project/docling.rs/master/scripts/install/download_dependencies.sh | sh # anywhere ``` Every asset and option (ASR presets, enrichment models, NER for PII redaction, INT8, fonts), GPU execution providers and the environment overrides: [`docs/MODELS.md`](./docs/MODELS.md).
